title: Rahul Gandhi Calls Political Opponents 'Fascists' at Bharat Summit in Hyderabad
excerpt: Addressing the valedictory session of the Bharat Summit 2026, the Leader of the Opposition said fascists 'jump out of the woodwork when systems collapse' and launched a social security scheme for Telangana gig workers.
body:
• Rahul Gandhi addressed the valedictory session of the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad on Saturday, alongside Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy.
  • He described opponents in politics, business and academia as "fascists" who, he said, shout and refuse to listen while the majority stays humble and quiet.
  • Gandhi also launched the Telangana Gig Workers' Social Security and Welfare Scheme, with Rs 5 lakh accident insurance, Rs 10 lakh health insurance and a pension contribution of 1% of earnings.
  • Outside the venue, BJP youth workers protested and the party's Telangana president said he had been placed under house arrest to stop the demonstrations.

Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi used the closing session of the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad on Saturday to attack what he called the rise of "fascists" in politics, business and academia, telling delegates that such figures emerge when institutions fail.

"You find people at the head of businesses; you find them in academics, they know it all, and in politics we call them fascists. Fascists tend to scream. They shout, they scream, they don't listen. The majority listens, pays attention, is humble, so the fascists tend to have a louder voice," Gandhi said during his address at the Hyderabad International Convention Centre, according to Khel Ja's report of the speech.

"Historically, the fascists jump out of the woodwork when systems collapse. And for the last decade, the fascists have been running, romping, jumping, shouting, screaming."

— Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition

A summit that became a political contest

The two-day summit, held on November 13 and 14 and jointly organised by the Congress-led Telangana government and the Samriddha Bharat Foundation, was expected to draw around 1,000 delegates from about 70 countries, The Daily Jagran reported. The Congress presented it as a platform for democratic values, inclusive development and cooperation.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Dft_8Csjzfy/

The BJP opposed the event from the start. Its Telangana president, N Ramchander Rao, called the gathering an "Anti-Bharat Summit" and alleged it brought organisations hostile to India to the state. Rao said he was placed under house arrest at his Tarnaka residence on Saturday to prevent protests, described the action as illegal, and accused the Congress government of curbing the opposition's democratic right to protest. Workers of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha protested outside the venue, and the party demanded the release of detained workers.

The summit also drew controversy over a foreign delegate: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng, a reporter for the Oslo-based newspaper Dagsavisen, said she had received a visa and political clearance to attend as a panellist, but her visa was revoked before the event. Bharat Rashtra Samithi working president K T Rama Rao separately alleged that the state government was spending Rs 100 crore of public money on the summit.

A gig-worker scheme launched alongside the speech

Gandhi used the visit to launch the Telangana Gig Workers' Social Security and Welfare Scheme. Listing the benefits in a post on X, he said workers would receive Rs 5 lakh in accident insurance and Rs 10 lakh in health insurance, a pension contribution of 1% of their earnings, rights over their work-related data and earnings, and Wi-Fi-enabled rest centres at various locations.

He said the scheme fulfilled a promise made in 2023, when he met Telangana's gig workers and heard their demands for protection. "The promise was: your demands will be met, and you will definitely have protection," he said, adding that the provisions had now become legal rights for gig workers in the state.

What happens next

The immediate fallout is political rather than legislative: the BJP has demanded that restrictions on its state president be lifted and detained workers released, while the Congress government is presenting the summit and the gig-worker scheme as evidence of its governance model. For gig workers in Telangana, the practical question is how quickly the insurance, pension and rest-centre provisions are rolled out and how workers register for them.
